questions.stem: Human insulin is now produced by genetically modified bacteria. The process involves cutting the human insulin gene from human DNA and inserting it into bacterial DNA. Which enzyme is used to cut the insulin gene from the human chromosome?

options.text: DNA ligase
Amylase
A restriction enzyme
DNA polymerase

questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes are molecular scissors that cut DNA at specific base sequences. They are used to cut the desired gene from the donor organism's DNA. DNA ligase is then used to join (ligate) the gene into the bacterial plasmid. DNA polymerase copies DNA during replication, and amylase is a digestive enzyme - neither is involved in gene cutting.

questions.stem: Bt cotton is a genetically modified crop that contains a gene from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis, which produces a protein toxic to insect pests. What is the main advantage of growing Bt cotton for farmers?

options.text: Bt cotton grows faster than normal cotton
Bt cotton produces its own insecticide, reducing the need for chemical pesticide spraying and lowering costs
Bt cotton is resistant to all diseases
Bt cotton produces more colourful fibres

questions.explanation: Bt cotton produces the Bt toxin protein in its cells, which kills insect pests that eat the plant. This means farmers need to spray fewer chemical pesticides, reducing costs and environmental damage from pesticide use. The plants are not resistant to all diseases - only to specific insect pests that are susceptible to the Bt toxin.

questions.stem: In genetic engineering, a vector is needed to carry the desired gene into the host organism. Which of the following is commonly used as a vector?

options.text: A ribosome
A bacterial plasmid - a small circular piece of DNA
A chromosome from the host organism
An amino acid chain

questions.explanation: Bacterial plasmids are commonly used as vectors in genetic engineering. A plasmid is a small, circular piece of DNA that can be easily removed from bacteria, have a new gene inserted using restriction enzymes and ligase, and then be reintroduced into bacteria. The bacteria then read the inserted gene and produce the desired protein. Viruses can also be used as vectors.

questions.stem: Golden Rice has been genetically modified to produce beta-carotene (a precursor to vitamin A). It was developed to help prevent vitamin A deficiency in developing countries. Which is a valid concern raised by opponents of Golden Rice?

options.text: Golden Rice cannot grow in tropical climates
The modified genes could transfer to wild rice populations through cross-pollination, with unknown ecological consequences
Golden Rice produces toxic levels of vitamin A
Golden Rice is more expensive than vitamin supplements for every community

questions.explanation: A legitimate concern about GM crops is gene flow - the possibility that modified genes could transfer to wild relatives through cross-pollination. This could have unpredictable effects on wild plant populations and ecosystems. Other concerns include corporate control of food supply and potential unknown long-term health effects, though Golden Rice has been extensively tested for safety.

questions.stem: Before genetic engineering, insulin for diabetic patients was extracted from pig or cow pancreases. Why is genetically engineered human insulin preferred over animal insulin?

options.text: Human insulin is cheaper to produce than animal insulin

Human insulin is identical to the patient's natural insulin, reducing allergic reactions; it can be produced in large quantities reliably; and it is acceptable to patients with religious objections to animal products
Animal insulin does not work in humans at all
Genetically engineered insulin works faster than any natural insulin

questions.explanation: Genetically engineered human insulin has several advantages: it is chemically identical to natural human insulin (reducing the risk of immune reactions), it can be produced in unlimited quantities by bacterial fermentation, it does not require animal slaughter (addressing ethical and religious concerns), and the supply is more reliable. Animal insulin does work but can cause allergic reactions in some patients.
